title: The Determinant: Minors, Cofactors and Expansion
quickIdea: The determinant is one number attached to a square matrix; compute it by expanding along a row or column with alternating signs, choosing the line with the most zeros.
remember: The determinant is defined for square matrices only. For 2 x 2, |[[a,b],[c,d]]| = ad - bc.
The minor M_ij is the determinant left after deleting row i and column j; the cofactor is C_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij.
Laplace expansion along row i: |A| = sum over j of a_ij C_ij, and the same works along any column; the value does not depend on which line you pick.
A triangular matrix, upper or lower, including diagonal, has determinant equal to the product of its diagonal entries; |I| = 1 and |O| = 0.
|A| is the signed volume scaling of the map x -> Ax: zero means the map squashes space into a lower dimension, which is exactly singularity.

example.work: Expand along the first row, where only a_11 = 2 survives: |A| = 2 x |[[1,7,2],[0,2,0],[0,6,1]]|. Expand that along its first row: 1 x |[[2,0],[6,1]]| = 2. So |A| = 2 x 1 x 2 = 4.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2000 Q.1.3 is a one-mark question solved by two expansions because the first row is mostly zeros; choosing the sparse line is the whole technique.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Compute the determinant of [[3,0,0],[5,2,0],[1,7,4]].
variations.why: The matrix is lower triangular, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal, 3 x 2 x 4.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does expanding along a different row give the same determinant?
variations.answer: Because the determinant is a single number defined by the signed volume of the image of the unit cube, and each expansion is a different way of computing that same alternating sum.
variations.why: The expansion is a theorem about the determinant, not its definition, so the value cannot depend on the line chosen.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A is 4 x 4 with exactly one non-zero entry in its second column. Which line should you expand along, and how many 3 x 3 minors do you evaluate?
variations.answer: The second column, and just one minor.
variations.why: Every other term of that expansion is multiplied by a zero entry, so only the single non-zero term survives.

trap.what: Dropping the alternating sign, or using a minor where a cofactor is needed.
trap.why: The sign (-1)^(i+j) alternates in a checkerboard, and both the expansion and the adjoint are built from cofactors, not from minors.
trap.counterexample: For A = [[1,2],[3,4]] the minor M_12 is 3 but the cofactor C_12 is -3; using minors throughout would give adj(A) = [[4,2],[3,1]] instead of the correct [[4,-2],[-3,1]].

check.question: What is the determinant of [[2,5],[1,3]]?
check.explanation: ad - bc = 2 x 3 - 5 x 1 = 1, so the matrix is non-singular.
